analysis.title: Powering AI: Agents, Aircons, Allshoring: All Not Priced In
key_insights: MS says power tightness will exceed expectations as industrial and household demand join AI. It estimates powering everything unlocks US$0.5trn of value creation and lifts Street 2028e EPS by about 14%.
Global power consumption estimates are raised a further 10% above Street, to about 36trn units and a 4.2% CAGR through 2030. Growth outside China is expected to run 3x the historical pace.

2026-30 power demand growth estimates were raised in almost every region, led by India (+454bps), the US (+169bps) and Australia (+141bps). Europe and Japan are expected to see steady growth after years of decline.
Asia accounts for about 64% of global incremental power demand to 2030. MS says Asia's power supply needs to grow at about a 5% CAGR, roughly 140bps faster than the current average.

Allshoring is the largest driver of Asian demand. Industrial power consumption is forecast to grow at about a 4% CAGR, which is 43% of incremental demand and about 2.7x the growth rate of data center consumption.

Air conditioning is an underappreciated source of demand. Space cooling adds about 40bps to Asia's power demand growth through 2030 and could be nearly as large as incremental data center demand. Cooling's share of global electricity rises from 10.1% in 2025 to 12.0% in 2030e.
Agentic AI makes power a bottleneck. Cost per token is falling, but agentic workloads raise token consumption per task, and Asia has one of the fastest AI adoption curves.
Asia data center power demand is forecast to reach 84GW by 2030e, about 4x 2025 levels. It grows at a 27% CAGR in Asia versus 26% in the US, from both AI and non-AI workloads.
AI workloads drive most of the data center power increase in Asia and the US, while Europe lags.
After accounting for time-to-power solutions, US data center developers face a shortfall of 43GW by 2028 and 80GW by 2029. This pushes capacity overseas and behind the meter.

About 15GW of the US shortfall could spill over to Asia, led by ASEAN (about 8GW) and India. Hyperscalers and neoclouds have already contracted about 10.6GW of data center capacity in Asia, over 70% of it in India and ASEAN.

Behind-the-meter power demand is estimated to grow to 47GW in the US and 8GW in Asia by 2030, favoring onsite power providers. Fossil fuels hold about half of the 2030 generation mix in MS's forecast, and 60% of Asia's data center capacity runs on coal and natural gas.
Coal and energy storage compete with costlier imported natural gas at about US$50-60/MWh round-the-clock generation cost. MS says price-sensitive Asia needs generation to stay economical.

Duck curves (midday solar dips in net demand) are reshaping into double-humped camels, with demand rising before and after daylight. This lifts margins for flexible generators and batteries and reduces returns for renewables.

Surging demand, disrupted fuel supply and grid upgrades have lifted power prices about 20% YoY in 2026. MS sees merchant power spreads expanding about 15% by 2028e, and wholesale prices are turning up again after easing from the 2022 peak.
Pricing power is shifting from equipment suppliers to power infrastructure owners. Generators are seeing ASP increases after 18 months of inflation at equipment producers.

Power cost has one of the lowest earnings impacts for AI hyperscalers. A 20% change in power prices moves earnings only about 1%, which gives utilities room to capture higher tariffs. The 100MW model shows 93% EBITDA margin and 37% net margin.
MS says equities do not price this in. Asia Powering AI beneficiaries de-rated YTD despite earnings upgrades.
MS ranks power markets on demand growth, tightness, capacity growth, energy security, regulation and valuation. China scores 4.3, India 4.1, Malaysia 4.0 and the US 3.4. Japan scores lowest at 2.3.
Winners named: EDP and RWE in Europe. In Asia, Gulf Development, Keppel, Adani Power, Yangtze Power, Samsung SDI and Hokkaido Electric. In the US, Bloom Energy and Solaris Energy.
Names to avoid: KEPCO, Tata Power, Global Power Synergy, Huaneng Power and Electric Power Development in Asia, and Enagas and SNAM in Europe. Most are Underweight or Equal-weight.

sector_views.rationale: The US, ASEAN and India stack up best as demand outpaces baseload and grid capacity. The US overall score is 3.4.
India has the largest estimate raise (+454bps) and scores 4.1. Malaysia scores 4.0. Spare capacity is ramping up to absorb US data center spillover.
Both are improving after years of decline, with steady growth. Japan has the lowest market score at 2.3.
Coal and storage compete with costly imported gas in price-sensitive Asia. GAIL, Tokyo Gas and Osaka Gas are Equal-weight, and Enagas and SNAM are Underweight.
Behind-the-meter demand rises to 47GW in the US and 8GW in Asia by 2030, and pricing power shifts to power infrastructure owners.
MS industry view is In-Line for the coverage universe.

earnings_insights: MS estimates its power thesis lifts Street 2028e EPS by about 14% across the covered universe. This is a MS forecast, not a reported figure.
Asia Powering AI beneficiaries de-rated YTD despite earnings upgrades, per MS (valuations priced at 12 Oct 2026).

In the MS 100MW data center model, power cost is US$116mn against US$1,930mn revenue and US$714mn net profit. A 20% change in power prices moves hyperscaler earnings about 1%. These are MS model estimates.

macro_indicators.interpretation: MS raised its above-Street global power consumption estimate by 10%. Demand is inflecting across the US, Europe, Japan, LatAm and Asia.
Asia supplies about 64% of the incremental demand, which MS says supports tighter power markets and higher prices.
Supply must accelerate to meet demand, supporting asset owners and generators.
MS estimate of broad-based price inflation, supporting wider generator spreads.
Higher spreads favor merchant generators and flexible assets.
Air conditioning adds meaningful demand outside data centers.

macro_indicators.reading: 47GW in the US and 8GW in Asia
macro_indicators.interpretation: Grid constraints push data center developers to onsite power.
The shortfall pushes capacity overseas and behind the meter.
Demand for dependable power lifts the fossil share compared with the 2024 level of 44%.

trade_ideas.description: Own power infrastructure winners: EDP and RWE in Europe, Gulf Development, Keppel, Adani Power, Yangtze Power, Samsung SDI and Hokkaido Electric in Asia, Bloom Energy and Solaris Energy in the US.
trade_ideas.rationale: Power tightness outpaces expectations as industrial, cooling and AI demand join, and about half of the requirement is not priced into equities.

trade_ideas.description: Avoid KEPCO, Tata Power, Global Power Synergy, Huaneng Power, Electric Power Development, Enagas and SNAM.
trade_ideas.rationale: Grid operators in these names rank below peers on MS's scorecard and carry Equal-weight or Underweight ratings.

trade_ideas.description: Own onsite power providers as behind-the-meter demand rises to 47GW in the US by 2030.
trade_ideas.rationale: Grids stay constrained, so data center developers bring their own power.

risk_factors: Hyperscaler power demand relies on AI token consumption, and MS notes token consumption is outpacing agentic revenues.
Price-sensitive Asian markets need generation to stay economical, and imported gas is costlier than coal and storage at about US$50-60/MWh.
Renewables see lower returns as duck curves reshape into double-humped camels.
The report states that power equipment producers saw ASP inflation over the last 18 months before pricing power shifted to infrastructure owners.
Morgan Stanley discloses investment banking relationships with many of the covered companies, which MS says may affect objectivity.
charts_described: Exhibit 1: 2026-2030 power demand growth CAGR by region with change in estimates vs 2025 in bps, including India +454, US +169, Australia +141, SE Asia +130, Europe +72, Japan +53 and China -81.
Chart of global cooling power demand (TWh) shows cooling share of global electricity rising from 10.1% in 2025 to 12.0% in 2030e.
Chart on how the IEA 2030 power mix forecast evolved shows total fossils at 49% in MSe 2030 versus 54% in the IEA 2019 forecast and 44% in 2024.
Global power demand bridge 2025-2030 runs from 29,654 to 36,346 Bn units, with China adding 2,984 and Asia ex-China 1,272.
India net load curves for May and January compare 2023, 2025 and 2026 and show the duck curve getting deeper while its shape keeps evolving.
vol_and_positioning: Positioning read: Asia Powering AI beneficiaries de-rated YTD despite earnings upgrades, and MS says equities are not pricing the power thesis in. No volatility or flow data is given.
geopolitical: Energy security is named as a driver of the power thematic, alongside AI and an industrial capex supercycle.
Disrupted fuel supplies are cited as one cause of the 2026 rise in power prices.
Allshoring of industrial activity is a named driver of Asian industrial power demand.
US and China hyperscalers and neoclouds are contracting data center capacity in Asia, led by India and ASEAN.
